newsitem.title: CHINA: SOME CHINA OFFICIALS WANT FOREIGN FIRM TAX BREAKS.
newsitem.headline: SOME CHINA OFFICIALS WANT FOREIGN FIRM TAX BREAKS.

text.p: China may be reconsidering a decision to scrap tax holidays on imports of capital goods by foreign firms after an outcry from several southern China provinces, the official China Daily said on Thursday.
"In view of a widespread outcry of concern and strong petition from some provinces, some readjustment measure could be already in the pipeline," the newspaper said.

Authorities in southern Guangdong province feared that withdrawing tax-free treatment of imports of capital goods for foreign firms would hamper their drive to attrach more high-technology projects with foreign funding, the newspaper said quoting a provincial official.
Officials in eastern Jiangsu province and the city of Shanghai had voiced similar concerns about the problem, the unidentified official said.

China said last year that foreign-funded firms with projects worth less than $30 million would lose their tax privileges by the end of this year while projects worth more than $30 million would lose the holidays by the end of 1998.
Beijing recently announced a six-month extension on the tax breaks.
